title: Claudio Carsughi, sports journalist, dies at 93
seoTitle: Claudio Carsughi, Iconic Sports Journalist, Dies at 93
subtitle: Claudia Carsughi's father dies after 27-day hospitalization
excerpt: Claudio Carsughi, a prominent figure in sports journalism, passed away this Thursday at 93, after a 27-day hospitalization for a respiratory infection.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Claudio Carsughi, a sports journalist with a long career, died this Thursday at the age of 93, after 27 days of hospitalization due to a respiratory infection. The news was announced by his daughter, Claudia Carsughi, in an Instagram post.

What Changed in Your Pocket When the Journalist Passed Away

Carsughi's passing brought to light the trajectory of a professional who worked for over seven decades, covering five consecutive World Cups and excelling in motorsports and Formula 1.

How Claudio Carsughi Started in Journalism

He was born in Arezzo, Italy, on October 13, 1932, and moved to Florence as a child. In 1946, with his family, he arrived in Brazil, where he studied at Colégio Dante Alighieri in São Paulo, and later graduated with a degree in Civil Engineering from the Polytechnic School of USP. At 16, he was already working as a correspondent for the Italian newspaper “Corriere dello Sport,” participating in the coverage of the 1950 World Cup, held in Brazil.

Career in Radio and Television

In 1957, he began a nearly six-decade relationship with Jovem Pan, where he covered five consecutive World Cups (1970, 1974, 1978, 1982, and 1986). He also worked for radio stations Bandeirantes and Record, and had stints at Rádio Nacional and TV Brasil. On television, he worked for ESPN Brasil, commenting on “Linha de Passe,” and for SporTV, in addition to collaborating with TV Brasil.

Work in Motorsports and Formula 1

Carsughi was the technical director of “Quatro Rodas” magazine between 1974 and 1990, executive editor of “Oficina Mecânica,” and founder of “Auto&Técnica.” He tested the Volkswagen Gol and drove a Ferrari Testarossa in 1992. In motorsports, he became one of the country's most respected commentators on Formula 1, focusing on mechanics, engines, and team strategies.

Legacy and Tribute

In 2023, he was honored by the Legislative Assembly of the State of São Paulo for his career and contribution to Brazilian journalism and motorsports. His daughter, Claudia Carsughi, published a text on the family's portal highlighting her father's ethics, surgical objectivity, and integrity, calling him “Master Carsughi.”

With information from UOL, O GLOBO, Jovem Pan.
